title: Add stable dtype and device PyObject conversions and an is_tensor probe (2.14+)
body:
Follow-up to #183323, extending the Python interop shims with dtype/device conversions and a tensor type-check probe, using the same `PyObjectConversionInterface` vtable mechanism (no new machinery).

## Summary
- Add `torch::stable::{dtype_from_pyobject,dtype_to_pyobject}` (`torch.dtype` <-> `ScalarType`) and `torch::stable::{device_from_pyobject,device_to_pyobject}` (`torch.device` <-> `torch::stable::Device`), gated at 2.14, in `torch/csrc/stable/pyobject.h`
- Add `torch::stable::is_tensor_pyobject`: probes whether a Python object is a `torch.Tensor` (or a subclass). `tensor_from_pyobject` errors on non-tensors, so code that receives arbitrary Python objects (e.g. argument conversion in a Python-registered custom op) needs a way to check first; the non-stable equivalent `THPVariable_Check` requires libtorch_python, and checking from Python via `isinstance` costs a Python round-trip per argument
- Backing C shims (`torch_is_tensor_pyobject`, `torch_dtype_from_pyobject`, `torch_dtype_to_pyobject`, `torch_device_from_pyobject`, `torch_device_to_pyobject`) in `torch/csrc/stable/c/shim.h` + `torch/csrc/shim_common.cpp`; no handle type involved — a dtype crosses the ABI boundary as the `int32_t` code already used by `aoti_torch_dtype_*()`, a device as a `(device_type, device_index)` `int32_t` pair in the `aoti_torch_device_type_*()` encoding; codes are translated through `torch::stable::detail::from`/`to` like the existing `Tensor::scalar_type()`/`device()` accessors
- Implementations in libtorch_python via `THPVariable_Check`, `THPDtype`/`torch::getTHPDtype` and `THPDevice`/`THPDevice_New`; like the tensor shims they require libtorch_python loaded at runtime and the GIL held, and the no-op default errors with a clear message in a libtorch-only process (also for the probe — a silent `false` would mask libtorch_python missing)
- The C shims validate dtype/device codes at the boundary before narrowing (an out-of-range code, e.g. device_index=256, errors instead of silently wrapping through the int8-backed c10 types)
- The header-only helpers translate through the stable enum mappings (`torch::stable::detail::from`/`to`), which cover a subset of ScalarTypes / DeviceTypes; a valid `torch.dtype` / `torch.device` outside that subset errors (documented in `pyobject.h` and the stable ABI note)
- Document the new APIs in the Python interop shims section of the LibTorch stable ABI note

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m pytest test/cpp_extensions/test_libtorch_agnostic.py -k pyobject -v` — parametrized roundtrips (7 dtypes incl. float8; cpu/meta/cuda/cuda:1 devices, incl. an index-less device that must not come back as cuda:0), end-to-end `Tensor::scalar_type()`/`device()` -> Python object, the probe on tensors / a tensor subclass / non-tensors, error cases for non-dtype/non-device inputs
- [x] `test_shim --gtest_filter="TorchPyObjectConversion.*"` — 6 tests: no-op fallback returns `AOTI_TORCH_FAILURE` (not a crash) without libtorch_python, and out-of-range dtype/device codes are rejected with clear errors

---
